card-title.purpose: A cat's or relic's name on its piece, the points tag, token counts, reward-step numerals.

body.purpose: Page and dialog copy, and what is typed in a field.

body-sm.purpose: In-game prose: the prompt in the turn block, the rival's last card, result lines, table rows. The event log sets its lines at 13px.

caption.purpose: Rules text on a card, a goal on a round tile, relic text, score sheet lines, italic flavor text.

label.purpose: Sentence-case heading above a group of pieces, the label beside a row of filter tokens (soft ink), the second line of a lane's activate tile, small table button text.

piece-label.purpose: Text on a piece, 11px, ink, bold or black: lane-tile names from 640px, space costs, You and Rival above a score, the Boss tag, the Info button.

piece-label-sm.purpose: The floor, 10px: a lane-tile name on a phone, a die's element name, a key hint, and below 640px the Fires 1st mark and the cat's name in the landing demo.

print.purpose: Jersey 20 at 20px, on every page: lane names, Round n, the rival's name, tier names, gauntlet numerals, the log heading, score totals. In the codex a section's count and the name of a relic and a rival. On the landing page also a rival's name and numeral in the rival fan and the lane's name in the lane showcase's readout.

print-lg.purpose: Jersey 20 at 30px: the title of a board and of a dialog, the two counts on home's codex board, run screen headings and the two score tokens. Also a page's one heading below 640px.

print-xl.purpose: Jersey 20 at 40px from 640px: the one h1 of a page outside a run (the ribbon on the landing page and on home, Codex, the sign-in heading, the 404) and each panel's h2 on the landing page. 30px below 640px.

wordmark.purpose: The die-cut wordmark on the title plaque: 56px, 76px from 640px, 96px from 1024px on the landing page; 48px, 64px from 1024px on home, where it is left out below 640px. Weight 800, line-height 0.9, tracking -0.035em, with a 3px ink stroke painted under the fill and a 3px chipboard edge and a 2px ink line as a straight-down text shadow. Mon is coral.

lid-wordmark.purpose: The wordmark on the lid of every signed-in page and of login and signup: cream with Mon in coral, not cut. 1.25rem below 640px. The pull quote in the landing page's cast panel takes the same two sizes at 700 in italics.

shadows.name: rarity-band
shadows.purpose: Strip across the top of a cat card; an inset band, not a shadow.

shadows.name: piece
shadows.value: 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + 2px) 0 -2px #b9a47e, 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + 2px) 0 0 #17212b, 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + var(--lift, 0px) + 7px) 0 -2px var(--cast)
shadows.purpose: Every piece on every page: the chipboard edge, the ink line under it, and a cast that shows 3px at rest. --e is 2px for a token or tile and 3px for a card; a piece printed on a piece has none.

shadows.name: pack-edge
shadows.value: five flat strips under one sawtooth mask (teeth 16px across, 8px deep, 2px steps), moved by translateY: chipboard by E, ink by E + 2px, cast by E + L + 5px; steps(2, end) over 120ms
shadows.purpose: What a pack in the shop has in place of the piece shadow, which cannot follow its crimped edge: the cut line and the wrapper inside it, and under the bottom crimp the edge, the ink line and the cast, read off the piece's own --e, --lift and --sink. A pack stands 8px (E), the pile of its sixteen cards; a stack of copies stands 3px plus 1px for each copy under the top one.

shadows.name: mat
shadows.purpose: The sky mat as a 3px board on the cloth: the match's player mat (a cost strip over three lanes printed with their habitats), and the menu mat on home.

shadows.name: tray-well
shadows.purpose: A recess, shaded along its top inner edge.

shadows.name: rail
shadows.purpose: The docked edge of a match and the phone's nav dock, shading the cloth above the ink line. The rail down the side of a match has an ink line and no shade.

shadows.name: cast-cloth
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the cloth or on a board.

shadows.name: cast-mat
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the mat.

shadows.name: cast-rail
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the docked edge, the match's side rail or the phone's nav dock.

shadows.name: stage
shadows.purpose: The cobalt stage frame as a 5px board with a 5px cast in the colour of what it stands on: on the landing page and around the sign-in picture.

shadows.name: board
shadows.purpose: Every board: a page's, a dialog's, the landing page's folded board and the board in its close. A 3px board like the mat. --board-cast is deep sky on a sky band, #0b1118 under a dialog, and ink at 60% in deep stone in the tower's room.

shadows.name: hero-mat-edge
shadows.purpose: The lower edge of the full-bleed sky mat on the cloth, under a 2px ink bottom border.

shadows.name: fold
shadows.purpose: The shade on the far side of a seam between two panels of the board, under a 2px ink top border.

shadows.name: wordmark-edge
shadows.purpose: The wordmark's letters as die-cut pieces, on the landing page's plaque and on home's.

shadows.name: crowd-cast
shadows.value: a bar under the sprite: height 6.25%, inset 18.75% left and right, background var(--cast)
shadows.purpose: The flat cast of a standing crowd cat or oversized icon, and of the player's hadu on home's menu mat and on the profile's: one sprite pixel deep.

shadows.name: cast-sky
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece or a board on a sky band.

shadows.name: cast-lid
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the ink lid and the landing footer, and of a dialog on the dimmed page.

shadows.name: field
shadows.purpose: A text field: a white slot cut into the board, shaded along its top inner edge.

shadows.name: cast-room
shadows.purpose: What a board casts on the stone wall inside the tower (the codex).

shadows.name: dialog-scrim
shadows.purpose: The dimmed page under a dialog. A flat fill, not a shadow and not a blur.

shadows.name: blank
shadows.purpose: The fill of a chipboard blank where something is still to be printed. No border and no shadow.

shadows.name: cast-scene
shadows.purpose: What a piece, a board and a mat cast on a page laid over the tower's scene (home, the 404): --cast, --board-cast and --mat-cast under .tower-app[data-place=outside] > .shell-page.

shadows.name: shelf-edge
shadows.value: not a box shadow: a strip 14px deep, #b9a47e between two 2px #17212b lines, behind the packs' feet
shadows.purpose: The shop's shelf, a board seen edge-on. Every pack hangs its price tag on its lip.

motion.name: demo-step
motion.value: 560ms between steps; 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The landing demo lands a turn one step at a time: the firing slot takes slot-fire, its line in the power list fills lime, and the rival's last card takes card-flip and is coral for that step. The landing page makes no sound.

motion.name: table-lift
motion.value: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); box-shadow 120ms steps(2, end); lifted translateY(-4px), hover translateY(-2px) for fine pointers, pressed translateY(2px)
motion.purpose: a piece lifts when chosen, rises on hover, sinks when pressed. The move eases with a little give; the edge and cast under it change in two steps and are never eased.

motion.name: hand-raise
motion.value: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); a hand card loses its lean (up to 9deg) and its drop (up to 28px) and rises to stand 12px clear of the bottom edge
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a card in the fanned hand stands upright and whole when hovered, focused or chosen. Its neighbours do not move.

motion.name: hand-lean
motion.value: perspective(40rem) rotateX/rotateY up to 5deg toward the pointer; transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); mouse only
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a raised hand card leans toward a mouse held over it. Flat on touch and under reduced motion.

motion.name: pack-turn
motion.value: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25) on the slot; pack-grow scale(0.6667) to 1 and pack-shrink scale(1.5) to 1, 220ms on the same curve, transform-origin 50% 100%; filter brightness(0.58) saturate(0.6) on a copy past the row's end, 220ms steps(2, end)
motion.purpose: The shop's row of packs turning. The row is a ring drawn as a strip of places, so every pack moves one place along and none crosses: the pack that goes off one end slides out into shadow as its copy slides in at the other. The pack that changes size is drawn at its new size at once and scaled from the old one, so the swap is hidden under one move. Nothing grows on load.

motion.name: pack-hover
motion.value: translateY(-4px) for the pack in the middle, -2px at the side, 150ms on the curve with give; a press sinks 2px; lean up to 5deg as hand-lean
motion.purpose: A pack under a mouse. The hover is bound on the slot the pack stands in, which does not move, so a pack that rises cannot leave the pointer. Touch and reduced motion leave it flat.

motion.name: pack-shine
motion.value: 520ms linear, once; a 34% wide band of white at 50%, skewX(-18deg), translateX(-160%) to 360%
motion.purpose: The one flat band of light that crosses the pack in the middle when a mouse comes onto it: the fourth and last light on the tabletop. No gradient. Not shown under reduced motion.

motion.name: pack-hop
motion.value: 360ms steps(1, end), once; translateY by one pattern unit (6px) and back
motion.purpose: The mascot on the pack in the middle hops one of its own pixels as a mouse comes onto the pack, in whole steps, as a sprite moves.

motion.name: stack-deal
motion.value: piece-land 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 24ms apart
motion.purpose: A pack's stacks dealt onto the mat when its cards are opened. None under reduced motion.

motion.name: stack-fan
motion.value: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); each lower copy 2px further out and rotate(2deg) more, about the foot of the stack
motion.purpose: The copies under a stack's top card coming out under a mouse or on focus. Still under reduced motion.

motion.name: card-step
motion.value: card-next translateX(16px) to 0, card-prev translateX(-16px) to 0; 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: In the pack viewer, the card turned to comes in from the side it was on. None under reduced motion.

motion.name: table-step
motion.value: 380ms for the first power, each next one 12% shorter, floor 180ms; 440ms for the player's own move, 540ms for the rival's card, 760ms for a scored goal, 1000ms for the end of a match
motion.purpose: Tabletop: an answered turn is played back one frame at a time and a chain speeds up as it runs; any click or key skips to the end, finishing every animation and cutting every sound.

motion.name: table-flight
motion.value: 300ms; cubic ease-out along a slight arc (up to 36px), sampled into 11 keyframes; the landing piece squashes 9% and springs back
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a played card or taken dice travel to where they land.

motion.name: piece-land
motion.value: 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); from translateY(-7px), 1px past, back
motion.purpose: A token arriving drops into place. Also the sign-in board, a notice, and the boards, mats and header pieces of a page set down after the camera has stopped.

motion.name: slot-fire
motion.value: 380ms ease-out; lime fill, translateY(-4px) scale(1.07) and back; returns to cream over 520ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The landing demo: the cat whose power is firing lights lime and makes one small jump. The match table uses slot-pop for the jump instead.

motion.name: slot-pop
motion.value: sampled spring, about 400ms (stiffness 960, damping 28); translateY(-4px) scale(1.07) rotate(1.6deg), each multiplied by 1 + 0.12 for every power before it, up to 8
motion.purpose: Match table: a cat pops as its power fires, harder the longer the chain, and starts over if it fires twice running. The lime fill is the is-firing class.

motion.name: token-punch
motion.value: sampled spring, about 240ms (stiffness 1750, damping 46); scale to 1.16 and back
motion.purpose: Match table: a food token, a cat or a score that just changed takes a hit. A power that changed nothing shrugs translateX(3px) on the same curve.

motion.name: score-float
motion.value: 720ms; springs out from scale(0.6), rises 34px, fades over the last 30%
motion.purpose: Match table: points scored rise off a cat as a lime chip, and off the rival's total as a coral one. At most 4 a frame.

motion.name: pixel-sparks
motion.value: 420 to 600ms; 4px squares thrown out 24 to 78px and falling 22 to 40px, fading over the last 40%
motion.purpose: Match table: a burst from a cat that scored, a won goal, a won match. At most 12 a frame, 6 under 640px.

motion.name: number-roll
motion.value: 70ms a step, 140ms to 520ms, cubic ease-out; written by a frame timer, not by React
motion.purpose: Tabletop: counts and scores roll to a new value instead of jumping. Set at once under reduced motion.

motion.name: score-heat
motion.value: opacity and scale 260ms; a deep-lime radial gradient behind the player's score, 0 at two powers into a chain and full at eight
motion.purpose: Match table: light that deepens behind the player's total as a chain runs. One of the four lights on the tabletop.

motion.name: table-shake
motion.value: sampled spring, about 400ms (stiffness 4900, damping 28); translate up to 3px by 1.5px, doubled for a lost match
motion.purpose: Match table: the mat and the supply jolt on a big hit, deep in a chain, on a raid or a burn, on a lost goal or match. The table itself never moves.

motion.name: result-tally
motion.value: 320ms, then one line every 190ms; the total punches 160ms after the last line, with a burst on a win
motion.purpose: The result sheet straight after a match counts the player's lines up in turn. Not on a reload, not on coming back to it.

motion.name: card-shimmer
motion.value: 2200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) infinite; one white band translated across the face
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a legendary in the hand catches the light while it stands up. One of the four lights; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: cloth-light
motion.value: 26s ease-in-out infinite alternate; a faint white radial patch the size of the screen, translated 16% by 9%
motion.purpose: The run route: a slow light drifting on the cloth, under every piece. One of the four lights; still under reduced motion; absent from the landing page.

motion.name: card-flip
motion.value: 380ms cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.3, 1); scaleX 1 to 0.04 to 1.04 to 1
motion.purpose: Tabletop, the landing demo included: the rival's card turns over and comes back coral.

motion.name: die-roll
motion.value: 340ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), each die 30ms after the last; from translateY(-9px) rotate(-120deg), a small bounce
motion.purpose: Tabletop: rerolled dice tumble in one after another.

motion.name: rival-hold
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the rival's last card stays coral after it turns, with or without motion.

motion.name: climb-step
motion.value: as played, each written length times the pace: 300ms opening pose; 500ms camera push or a window shutting; 750ms up the wall; 300ms landing; 275ms a floor of the tilt; 525ms a rival rising (450ms more on a boss's dark window); 600ms the roof pennant; 1125ms the pull back; 500ms the title card
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb between matches is played one frame at a time, like a turn.

motion.name: climb-pace
motion.value: 1.25: CLIMB_PACE in src/components/run/climb.ts, read by the stylesheet as --pace; every climb duration is calc(<written ms> * var(--pace)); the rests are not scaled
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the one number that sets how slowly the climb plays.

motion.name: climb-hop
motion.value: as played: transform 700ms steps(8, end) between ledges with a one-pixel scrabble left and right (175ms steps(1, end), four times), then the crowd's hop (450ms steps(1, end)) and two white dust pixels (350ms steps(3, end)) on landing; walking in at the foot is 20 pixels in 450ms steps(5, end)
motion.purpose: Tabletop: Hadu goes up one floor of the tower.

motion.name: climb-window
motion.value: transform 300ms steps(3, end) as played; translateY 100% dark, 37.5% looking over the sill, 0 out
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a rival slides up into its window.

motion.name: climb-camera
motion.value: one transform on the tower inside a clipped stage fixed over the whole window (inset 0, 100dvh): translate so the framed point sits at 50cqw and 44cqh, never further left than the window's edge, scale 1 (far back) or 2 (close); each beat's own duration, cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1); rounded to a whole pixel. One tower pixel is 2px, and 3px from 636 tall by 468 wide, 4px from 848 by 624, 5px from 1060 by 780, 6px from 1272 by 936
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb is shot like a scene. The camera pushes in on Hadu, follows him up the wall, crosses to the window, and pulls back at the roof.

motion.name: climb-bars
motion.value: two ink bars, 11cqh each, translateY from off the window's edge, 400ms as played, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); outside the box that shakes
motion.purpose: Tabletop: in whenever the climb's camera is close, out when it is far back.

motion.name: title-slam
motion.value: 425ms as played, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); from translateY(-36px) scale(1.12), past by 3px, settles; no fade
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb's title card (coral for a rival, lime at the roof) comes down over the lower bar on the last two beats.

motion.name: climb-rest
motion.value: 1400ms; 2200ms under reduced motion, where only the last frame is shown
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the last frame of a climb rests, then gives way to the next screen. Any click or key leaves at once.

motion.name: crowd-bob
motion.value: 1600ms steps(1, end) infinite; translateY(0) then translateY(-2px); animation-delay calc(var(--i) * -290ms)
motion.purpose: Landing page: each crowd cat and oversized icon idles on a 2px two-step bob, staggered so no two move together.

motion.name: crowd-hop
motion.value: 360ms steps(1, end), once; translateY 0, -10px, -14px, -6px, 0; animation-delay calc(var(--i) * 50ms); three times when the round is won
motion.purpose: Landing page: the crowd hops with the firing chain. The cluster right of the stage hops on the first slot to fire, the plaque's cat on the middle one, the left cluster on the last; every crowd cat hops three times when the round is won.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all animation and transition durations 0.01ms; the tabletop lands the whole turn at once with one settle sound, sets numbers at once, and skips flights, pops, floats, sparks, shakes, the hand lean, the shimmer, the cloth light and the result tally; the landing crowd's animations are removed and the demo's steps land with no delay; the shop's packs neither grow, lean, shine nor hop, a pack's stacks are simply on the mat and do not fan, and a card turned to is simply there A pack that is opened is its cards face up at once, and the chest is open with its relics there.
motion.purpose: Applied under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: blank-wait
motion.value: 900ms steps(3, end) infinite alternate; opacity 1 to 0.45
motion.purpose: A chipboard blank waits in steps, as a sprite would.

motion.name: place-move
motion.value: 360ms cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1); one transform on the tower's world
motion.purpose: The camera between outside (home, the 404) and the door (Play). moveMs and moveEase in src/components/tower/places.ts.

motion.name: room-move-in
motion.value: 480ms cubic-bezier(0.85, 0, 1, 0.3); zoom to 32
motion.purpose: The camera going in through The Archivist's window to the codex. It starts slowly, since magnifying by 32 is otherwise over in its first tenth. The wall cuts in when it stops.

motion.name: room-move-out
motion.value: 480ms cubic-bezier(0, 0.7, 0.15, 1); zoom from 32
motion.purpose: The camera coming out of the room. The wall cuts away at the press and the move ends slowly.

motion.name: page-land
motion.value: piece-land 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) on every .board, .mat and header piece of the page, together (the codex's book does not land: see room-enter); the landed state is held 320ms; one settle sound
motion.purpose: A page is put away (visibility: hidden) at the press and set down when the camera has stopped and the page has come, whichever is later.

motion.name: room-enter
motion.value: 640ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (ENTER_MS): the room starts as the deep stone the window's dark is, and a wash of it over the wall goes from opacity 1 to 0 while the wall, drawn 8% larger than the stage on every side, comes from scale(0.88) to 1; the shut book comes from opacity 0 and scale(0.94) with it
motion.purpose: Coming into the codex. The camera stops on the window's dark and the room comes up out of that same dark, still drifting closer, so there is no cut. The one place something fades in. Leaving is a cut. None of it under reduced motion.

motion.name: book-open
motion.value: 420ms beat once the book has come up (BEAT_MS after ENTER_MS), then the cover as the lifting leaf of a turn at 1.3 times a page's length (COVER_PACE): 286ms a half on a spread, 390ms on a single page; on a spread the shut book starts translateX(-25%) and moves over across both halves on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The codex comes up shut and opens by itself on every visit, once the camera has stopped. Constants in src/components/codex/turn.ts. Under reduced motion the book is open at once.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.value: two half-turns about the spine that meet edge-on: rotateY 0 to 90deg in 220ms on cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.9, 0.55), then the facing page 90deg to 0 in 220ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); a single page is one half of 300ms; perspective 2800px at the spine (1800px at a single page's left edge); a flat ink wash to 24% on the moving leaf and 12% on the page under it
motion.purpose: A page of the codex turns. No page is seen from behind, so there is no preserve-3d and no backface. One leaf whatever the distance; the latest request wins. A cut under reduced motion.

motion.name: tab-out
motion.value: 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25), each tab 40ms after the last; from translateY(100%) under the book's top edge, or translateX(100%) under its left edge from 1024px; the cats' filter flags the same from under the top edge, a group at a time, 60ms apart
motion.purpose: The codex's chapter tabs come out from behind the book once it lies open, and the cats' filter flags whenever the Cats chapter is turned to.

motion.name: card-pop
motion.value: Web Animations API on the dialog's board, transform only, one scale both ways, origin 0 0: from the pocket's box to rest in 300ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25), back in 220ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); popTransform in src/components/ui/pop.ts
motion.purpose: A cat taken out of its pocket in the codex comes up as its full card and goes back. Modal's origin and onClosed props; any other dialog is simply there and gone, and so is this one under reduced motion.

motion.name: move-limit
motion.purpose: A page that has not come by then is given up on and the page being left is shown again.

motion.name: scene-drift-far
motion.value: 336s steps(168, end) infinite; translateX by one 168-pixel tile, a tower pixel every 2s; none under reduced motion
motion.purpose: The far bank of cloud behind the tower drifts left in whole tower pixels and loops. Transform only.

motion.name: scene-drift-near
motion.value: 150s steps(120, end) infinite; translateX by one 120-pixel tile, a tower pixel every 1.25s; none under reduced motion
motion.purpose: The near bank of cloud, a little quicker.

motion.name: pack-open
motion.value: sealed 460ms; top strip off in 300ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (42% right, 20px up, 16deg, to clear), held 340ms; card back up 34% in 300ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25), held 380ms; then dealt
motion.purpose: A bought pack opening where it stood in the middle of the shelf. One flat band crosses it and its sticker hops once as the strip comes off. The rail's only action meanwhile is a cream Skip.

motion.name: pack-card-turn
motion.value: card-flip 380ms; back and face swap by visibility at 190ms; Turn them all: one card every 170ms
motion.purpose: Turning a dealt card face up: a press, Enter or Space, or the rail's Turn a card. The tag under it lands as a token does (240ms, after 190ms).

motion.name: climb-stroll
motion.value: translateX(-48 tower px) to 0, 700ms x pace, steps(10, end), with a one-pixel bob each 140ms x pace
motion.purpose: Hadu walking in over the landing as a run opens.

motion.name: climb-stumble
motion.value: a walk that lurches one pixel forward and three up at 80%, 700ms x pace, steps(1, end)
motion.purpose: Hadu stumbling onto the chest by the tower's foot.

motion.name: theft-fly
motion.value: from Hadu's pack to a window's middle in steps(8, end), 480ms x pace, from 180ms and 70ms apart x pace, hidden at the end
motion.purpose: The stolen cards going up one after another into the rivals' windows.

motion.name: chest-lid
motion.value: translateY two pixels, one, then rest, 240ms x pace, steps(1, end)
motion.purpose: The jolt of the chest's lid going back, with the cache sound.

motion.name: chest-rise
motion.value: translateY(1rem) to rest, hidden until it starts, 320ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25), 120ms apart
motion.purpose: The three relics rising into the offer once the opening rests on the chest: hidden until their turn, then there and rising, never faded in.

breakpoints.name: dock
breakpoints.value: below 768px: the five ways about the app dock to the bottom edge; --dock-h is 4.75rem plus the safe area, and 0 from 768px

breakpoints.name: tower-px
breakpoints.value: 2px; 3px from 640px by 720px; 4px from 1280px by 940px; 5px from 1680px by 1160px; 6px from 2000px by 1370px (min-width and min-height)

breakpoints.name: shelf-roomy
breakpoints.value: container min-width 1088px on the pack stage: packs 20px apart, all seven whole; 16px, 24px from 480px and 40px from 900px below it

breakpoints.name: room-columns
breakpoints.value: 1024px: the deck board is a 392px column stuck beside the collection; the profile's plate, mat and status card are an 18rem column stuck under the lid

sound.name: source
sound.value: Web Audio API oscillators and filtered noise from recipes in src/components/run/sfx/recipes.ts; no audio files, no library
sound.purpose: Every sound effect in a run.

sound.name: chain-ladder
sound.value: major pentatonic from E4 (329.63Hz), one step a power, capped at step 12
sound.purpose: The pitch of a power climbs with the chain; a power that changed nothing plays a dull 185Hz note and does not climb.

sound.name: press
sound.value: every press on any page makes one sound: its handler's own, else the falling click (sine 760Hz to 560Hz) from a window listener in src/components/run/sfx/ClickSound.tsx; a cobalt table button and a move sent play confirm (triangle G5 then C6)
sound.purpose: Nothing pressed is silent, and nothing is heard twice.

sound.name: cat-voices
sound.value: src/components/run/sfx/voices.ts: a ladder of rungs a quarter of a semitone apart from A3 (220Hz), one pitch a cat and no two alike; contour by archetype, timbre by element (triangle, sine, square at 0.1 at most; no sawtooth, no noise); longer and ornamented by rarity; 0.45s at most
sound.purpose: A cat is heard in its own voice when it is chosen or turned over to read, and when it is taken out of its pocket in the codex.

sound.name: page
sound.value: noise only: a bandpass rising 1400Hz to 3800Hz at 0.11 over 160ms, and a lowpass pat falling 900Hz to 320Hz at 0.1, 350ms in
sound.purpose: A page of the codex turned, by a tab, a button, a key or a swipe.

sound.name: cover
sound.value: lowpass noise rising 520Hz to 1100Hz at 0.14 over 240ms with a sine falling 190Hz to 150Hz at 0.06; then settle, played by delay as the cover comes down, since no voice but win and loss may run past 0.5s
sound.purpose: The codex's cover opening by itself. The one effect on a page that a press did not cause, with the page landing.

sound.name: limits
sound.value: peak note gain 0.5; master gain 0.8 full, 0.28 quiet, 0 muted; one limiter; 14 voices at most; longest voice 1.6s
sound.purpose: A long chain cannot clip or pile up.

sound.name: music
sound.value: tracks in src/components/run/music/tracks.ts: bpm, root, scale and bars of four 16-step parts (lead, arp, bass, drums) written as scale degrees; scheduled a bar at a time 200ms ahead of the bar line; 400ms crossfade on a change of tune
sound.purpose: One tune per screen of a run (run start, chest, tower, roof, reward, run won, run lost), one theme per rival, and one menu tune for home, the codex and the 404; the opening hand plays the rival's theme without its lead and drums.

sound.name: music-limits
sound.value: peak note gain 0.14; music bus 0.8 under the master; not counted against the 14 voices and not cut by a skip
sound.purpose: An effect always sits on top of the tune, and a skip never chops it.

sound.name: control
sound.value: localStorage key hadumon:sound: full, quiet or muted; default full. localStorage key hadumon:music: on or off; default on
sound.purpose: The speaker, in the table's corner and on the lid, cycles the three and is the master of effects and music alike; the note button beside it turns the music alone off. Nothing plays in a hidden tab; a skip cuts every effect voice and plays one settle sound.

sound.name: rig
sound.value: src/components/SoundRig.tsx: ClickSound and HoverSound, mounted once in the root layout
sound.purpose: The click, the knock on nothing and the hover tick are heard on every page, landing and sign-in included. A second mount would tick twice.

sound.name: menu-tune
sound.value: track menu in src/components/run/music/tracks.ts: 88bpm, root F4, pentatonic, triangle lead, a rocking arpeggio and a bass, hat only; mounted in the shell by src/components/MenuMusic.tsx
sound.purpose: Home, the codex and the 404. It carries from page to page without starting over and crossfades with the table's music. useMusic has one owner at a time, so a leaving page cannot hush the arriving one. Landing, login and signup have no tune.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Pieces on a Cream Table"**

HaduMon is a board game laid out on a warm cream table, and the whole app is that table. There is one material: die-cut cardboard on a woven cream cloth. Everything a player can see or press is a piece of it: square corners, a 2px near-black border, a flat fill, a chipboard edge straight down, and an unblurred cast shadow. A cat card, a button, a text field, a dialog, a notice, and the navigation are all cut from the same card. There is no page chrome. Nothing is rounded, nothing has a hairline border, and nothing has a blurred shadow.

The scope is one class, `.tabletop`, and it is on the `body` (`src/app/layout.tsx`) together with the pixel face, so every page is cardboard and a dialog or a notice drawn on the body is cardboard like the rest. A run's table (`TableSurface`, on `/run`) is a tabletop of its own inside it, because it carries the fit and the layer its effects are drawn on. Outside a run a page is laid out at page scale from a few large things: an ink lid across the top, cream boards on the cloth, a sky mat, a cobalt stage frame. A board (`src/components/ui/Board.tsx`) is the page-sized cream sheet that everything else is set out on. It has a card's edge and cast but it is not a piece, so the buttons, cards and tiles on it keep their own edge.

The tower a run climbs is the app's backdrop. It stands behind every signed-in page that is not the table, showing the run as it stands, and each of those pages is a place at it: home is outside, with the whole tower in view; Play is the door, close on wherever the run has got to; the codex, the deck, the shop and the profile are rooms inside, reached through The Archivist's window. Going from one page to another moves a camera on the tower, and the page arrived at is set down when the camera stops. The tower stands on a rock in the sea under an evening sky, drawn in the same pixels, so home and the 404 are not on the cloth: they are pieces laid over that scene, as a title screen is. Nothing readable is set straight on the scene; it is always on a piece, a mat or a board. The cloth is still the ground of the landing page, of a run's table and inside a stage frame. The landing page, login and signup have no tower.

The match is a table you sit at, not a dashboard you read, and nothing of the app stands around it: a white rail down the left holds the rival and the rounds and, under an ink line, the player's turn (scores, food, prompt, confirm); the shared supply and the player's sky mat with three printed lanes lie on the cloth in the centre; a score sheet, the relics and the log stand in a slim column to the right; and the hand is held as a fan along the bottom edge. There are no panels, on the table or off it. Counts are tokens, piles, and cubes; what the board says about itself is printed on it in a pixel face.

The cats are 16x16 pixel sprites: chibi, front-facing, a near-black outline, three fur tones taken from the cat's element, and eyes tinted by rarity. Two are drawn from life and wear their own colours: Hadu, a black-and-white tuxedo with a pink nose, and Stussy, a ginger. Of the 102 cats, 75 are put together from a library of parts, one part to a zone of the grid, in one of their element's four coats (`src/components/sprites/cats.ts`, `palettes.ts`). They are drawn as inline SVG and scaled in whole pixels. The tabletop adds a small set of 8x8 pixel icons drawn the same way (yarn, a coin, a pack, die, paw, den, card, cached, tucked, goal, chevron, and for the lid and the table's corner buttons a speaker at full, quiet and off, two beamed notes and one note crossed out, home, play, book and exit), the seven food icons (beef, fish, chicken, dry food, pork, a treat, and a question mark for a cost any food pays), and the five element marks (flame, drop, bolt, leaf, crescent). The fifteen relics have a drawing each, on the cats' 16x16 grid in the icons' outline and one fill: the five charms are one pendant on a cord holding their element's mark, and the other ten are the thing they are named for (a steaming saucer, a ball of twine with a loose end, a whisker pad with a kinked whisker, a folded map, a buttoned cushion, a sun on the horizon, a collar and its tag, a ringing bell, a basket of yarn, a bed in a room's corner). The six rivals are sprites too, on the cats' grid and all in the rival coral, each told apart by what it wears; they are met at the windows of the tower a run climbs, which is drawn in the same pixels in four stone greys and stands behind the rest of the app. Sprites, these icons, the tower and the scene it stands in are the only imagery. There are no photographs, no raster creature art, no gradients, and no emoji.

Density follows the game. The table is compact (10px between zones, 6px between pieces) because every rule the player needs has to be on the card or the board. Home, the codex, and sign-in breathe more: boards 28px apart, 16 to 20px of padding inside one. Copy is dry and factual, in sentence case.

The public landing page (`src/components/landing/LandingPage.tsx`, shown at `/` to a signed-out visitor) is the one Persuade surface. It is the tabletop at page scale, laid out as the front of the game's box, with no shell and no tower. From the top: an ink lid strip with the two account buttons; a full-bleed sky mat printed with paws and yarn; on it a cream title plaque with the wordmark and Hadu perched on top, a lime ribbon carrying the h1, and a thick cobalt stage frame holding one playable Hunt round run by the real match engine; a crowd of cats standing around the frame; then one cream board on the cloth, folded into four panels (the lead, the cats, the rows, the rivals); a sky closing band; and an ink footer. It is built from the table's own pieces (cat cards, dice, food tokens, the mat, tray wells, nameplates, turn cubes, score tokens, table buttons). It was the first page laid out at page scale, and the furniture it brought (the lid strip, the plaque and ribbon, the stage frame, the board, the crowd) is now the whole app's.

There are coins, packs and looks, and none of them is for sale. A finished run pays coins; coins open packs in the shop; packs fill the collection a deck is built from and dress the player's hadu, board, cloth, tower and sky. Coins are only ever earned by playing and the game takes no money, and every surface that shows a coin or a pack says so in a plain sentence: the shop's board, the Coins step of a run's summary, the landing page's close. A coin is one pixel icon in gold beside a numeral, and there is no other money on any page: no price in a currency, no payment control, no premium finish. A look changes colours and a weave; it never changes a rule or how a piece is built.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream cloth under the table and the landing page; sky blue for mats and bands; an evening sky and sea behind home.
One material: square 2px-ink cardboard pieces with a straight-down edge and an unblurred cast, on every page and in every dialog.
A board is the page-sized cream sheet that pieces are set out on. It is not a piece.
The grey pixel tower stands behind every signed-in page but the table, and those pages are places at it: outside, the door, a room.
Cobalt is the action, lime is the player's, coral is the rival's, ink is the act that cannot be undone.
16x16 pixel cats, rivals and relics, 8x8 pixel icons and one grey pixel tower on its rock in a pixel sea, as inline SVG, the only imagery.
One rounded bold type voice, plus a pixel print face at 20px and 30px, and at 40px for a page's one heading.
The landing page is the front of the box: lid strip, sky mat, title plaque, lime ribbon, cobalt stage frame, a crowd of cats, one folded cream board.
Every state has a border, fill, or height change, never colour alone on text.
Coins are earned at the table and nowhere else, and nothing is sold for money: wherever coins or packs are shown, a sentence says so.
A player's look repaints the board, the cloth, the tower's stone and its sky, and never how anything is built.

rules.name: The Lime Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Lime marks something the player chose, holds, or won, and where the player is: the page you are on, a filter you set. It is never decoration and never the rival's. One exception is named: the ribbon under the wordmark, on the landing page and on home, which carries the page's h1 and is lime although it is nothing the player chose, holds, or won. No other surface takes it.

rules.name: The Coral Is Theirs Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the rival and what the rival does, at the table and off it: a nameplate, a plate in the codex, the tag of a run a rival ended. It never marks a decision the player owes, never a piece the player owns, and never a destructive act: Log out and Abandon run are ink. Text sitting on a coral fill is ink.

rules.name: The Waiting Piece Rule
rules.body: A piece of the player's that is waiting on an answer takes a cobalt frame with a lime inner line. A card marked for trimming takes the cobalt chosen frame and an ink tag. Neither takes coral.

rules.name: The Ink On Colour Rule
rules.body: Text on lime, coral, sky, cream, white, or an element hue is ink. White text appears only on cobalt. Cream text appears only on ink: the lid, the landing footer, the small ink tag, the destructive button, and an error notice.

rules.name: The Element Stays On The Cat Rule
rules.body: Element hues colour sprites, food icons, element marks, and dice, the left edge of a cat's own card and tile, and the mark a charm holds. Boards, buttons, and headings never take an element colour. The sky behind the tower is the one place an element's colours are a ground, and a cat pack's wrapper is the one piece whose face they are.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Of Print Rule
rules.body: The pixel face is drawn on a 20px grid, so it is set at 20px and 30px and nowhere between. One step is added, for a heading only: 30px on a phone and 40px from 640px, on the one h1 of a page outside a run and on each panel's h2 on the landing page. Print is for what is printed (names, numerals, totals, headings), never for a sentence of rules text or copy, and never for anything typed: a field's text and its label are the rounded face. These are sizes at the table's own scale: a fitted run screen (see Layout) magnifies them with everything else on it.

rules.name: The Numbers Line Up Rule
rules.body: Every score, count, and cost that can change uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, buttons, labels, and tags are sentence case. Nothing in the build is set in uppercase: the filter group label and the Boss tag in the codex, once the two exceptions, are sentence case too.

rules.name: The Rules Are On The Piece Rule
rules.body: A card states its own cost, points, and power in words. Type on a piece may get small, but it stays ink and stays bold enough to read on a phone: 11px on a piece, 10px only for a lane-tile name on a phone, a die's name, and a key hint.

rules.name: The One Thickness Rule
rules.body: Every piece on every page has its edge and its cast, straight down and unblurred: on home, in the codex, at sign-in, in a dialog and in a notice as at the table. A piece printed on a piece has none of its own. A board is not a piece: it has a board's edge and cast, and the pieces on it keep theirs. No piece anywhere takes a blurred shadow or a sideways offset. One piece's outline is not four straight lines: a pack in the shop, crimped in a sawtooth along its top and bottom. Its edge and its cast follow the cut, and are still straight down and unblurred.

rules.name: The Frame Means State Rule
rules.body: A piece's state is its border: cobalt border for open to pick, cobalt border with a 2px cobalt inner line for chosen, cobalt border with a 2px cobalt and a 2px lime inner line for waiting on the player. A chosen piece is also lifted. No ring is drawn outside a piece's border. A pack is never chosen: the pack shown is the one in the middle of the row, and the marks under the row say which. A thing the account does not have is not a piece yet and has no frame: it is a dashed outline (see Shapes).

rules.name: The Three Heights Rule
rules.body: A thing on the table is print (0), a token or tile (2px), or a card (3px). Only a stack is taller, and its height is its count. The title plaque and the stage frame are the box's furniture, not things in play, and stand 5px.

rules.name: The Coin Is Earned Rule
rules.body: A coin is the pixel coin icon in gold beside a numeral in tabular figures, on a white or a cream piece. It is never a price in money. A surface that shows coins or packs says in one sentence where coins come from, as the shop does: "Coins are won at the table and nowhere else. Nothing here is sold for money."

rules.name: The Printable Look Rule
rules.body: A look changes colour and weave and never construction. Every board and every cloth is light enough to print on in ink (7:1), the inside of every tower is dark and its stone runs in four steps, and every sky runs one way from its palest at the sea to its top. `src/components/skins/skins.test.ts` holds it.

dos: Do make every new element a piece or a board. A piece: the `piece` class, square, 2px ink border, flat fill; the tabletop adds its edge and cast. A board: `Board`, the page-sized sheet that holds pieces.
Do leave the scope to the `body`, which is the tabletop. No page opens one of its own but a run's `TableSurface`, which needs the fit and the effects layer.
Do pick one of the three heights for a new thing on the table: print, token or tile (2px), card (3px).

Do render every cat through `src/components/PixelSprite.tsx` and every rival through `src/components/RivalSprite.tsx` at a whole-pixel multiple of 16 where the layout allows, every mark on a piece through `src/components/PixelIcon.tsx` at a multiple of 8, and every relic's drawing through `src/components/RelicIcon.tsx` at a multiple of 16.
Do use ink text on lime, coral, sky, cream, and white; white text only on cobalt; cream text only on ink.
Do show state on the table with the frame (cobalt border, cobalt inner line, lime inner line) and with height (lifted 4px, pressed 2px), and reinforce a chosen token with a lime fill.
Do end every choice in a run in the turn block or a rail, with a sentence saying what will happen and one cobalt table button.
Do give a sequence of screens a `StepRail` and keep its confirm on the last step alone; every earlier step only moves.
Do keep the run route free of the lid and the dock: the corner buttons are its only navigation.
Do lay a new column screen of a run in `TableArea` on a `TableSurface` with `fit`, and centre a short step with `fitted:my-auto`.
Do keep what names a hand card (sprite, points, cost, name, Info) in its left strip, and tilt only a card at rest; anything being read stands upright.
Do make every action from `TableButton` or `TableLink`: cobalt for the one way forward, cream for the rest, lime for the one of a set that is in force, ink for an act that cannot be undone.
Do set the pixel face at 20px or 30px, or at 40px for a page's one heading, and only for what is printed: a heading, a name, a numeral, a total.
Do give a page outside a run exactly one h1, in print at 30px, and 40px from 640px.
Do give every key a visible hint on its piece, shown only for a fine pointer, and keep every keyed action reachable by tap.
Do keep a page's controls at 44px tall or more where the layout allows; nothing interactive goes below 40px unless its hit area is extended.
Do write counts and scores in tabular figures and labels in sentence case.
Do give every loading surface blanks in the shape of its content, and every error a plain sentence and a retry.
Do build the landing page from the tabletop's own pieces (cat cards, dice, food tokens, the mat, tray wells, nameplates, table buttons), with no shell and no tower around them.
Do put a new signed-in page at a place (`placeFor` in `src/components/tower/places.ts`): the camera moves on the press, and the page lands when the camera has stopped.
Do keep the tower's side of a page clear where the page is outside (`beside-tower`), and lay a page in the room with `in-room` so its boards cast on stone.
Do draw scenery as rows of legend characters in tower pixels inside the tower's picture, and let the camera magnify it with the tower.
Do confirm a destructive act in a dialog, with the ink button beside a cream way back that holds the focus.
Do keep a crowd cat decorative: a whole multiple of 16, no label, no clicks, a flat cast only where it stands on the ground.

Do draw a lane's habitat as rows of legend characters (`sprites/habitats.ts`) in bands anchored to the lane's bottom edge, put every word and numeral in a lane on a plate or a piece, and build any mat from `src/components/mat/`.

Do let the window's size alone pick the match's layout: `fit-wide` from 1024 by 600px, `fit-compact` for a short window on its side, the turn prompt for a phone held upright, and otherwise the page that scrolls.
Do say where coins come from wherever a coin or a pack is shown, in one plain sentence: they are earned at the table and nowhere else, and nothing is sold for money.
Do show a coin as the pixel coin icon in gold (`COIN_COLOR`) beside a numeral in tabular figures, on a white or a cream piece.
Do render the player's hadu through `src/components/HaduAvatar.tsx` in a box that holds a whole multiple of 16, and leave its aura a quarter of the cat's edge on every side or cut it off.
Do draw a new thing to wear inside its slot's own cells of Hadu's grid (`HADU_SLOT_CELLS` in `src/components/sprites/hadu.ts`), and a new look in flat fills that pass `skins.test.ts`.
Do read a board's, a cloth's and the tower's colours through the properties a look sets (`--mat-fill`, `--mat-line`, `--cloth-fill`, the `--color-stone*` tokens), with the free look as the fallback.
Do show a piece of the wardrobe the account does not have as a dashed outline with its picture faint, and say where it is found.
Do let a change that costs nothing land at once and say so in one sentence that is read out (the wardrobe), and give a change that has to be kept one save and one sentence in a card rail (the deck).
Do put a new page that is a room in the tower in `in-room`, with its one h1 in print on a cream plate, as the codex, the shop and the profile have theirs.
donts: Don't round a corner anywhere, or draw a pill, a 1px hairline border, or a blurred shadow. The build has none.

Don't give a piece a blurred shadow, a diagonal offset shadow, or a glow. A piece has only the straight-down edge and cast. The only light on the tabletop is the four named under Motion: score heat, a raised legendary's shimmer, the drift on a run's cloth, and the one flat band that crosses a pack under a mouse or as it is torn open. An aura is drawn in pixels behind the hadu and is not a glow.
Don't give a board the `piece` class or lay a board on a board. A board is not a piece, and the pieces on it keep their own edge.
Don't bring back page chrome: no white panel, no side rail, no floating bar, no second kind of button.
Don't draw a ring outside a piece's border to show state.
Don't use coral for a decision the player owes, for a card the player is trimming, or for a destructive action. Coral is the rival's; Log out and Abandon run are ink.
Don't set the pixel face at any size but 20px and 30px, or 40px for a page's one heading, or use it for rules text, a sentence of copy, or anything typed.
Don't set readable text below 10px, or below 11px on a piece from 640px up.

Don't move a cardboard piece in steps, or a pixel sprite smoothly: pieces ease and spring, sprites hop a whole pixel at a time. The climb's camera moves the whole picture and is the one thing that eases a sprite across the screen. Don't fade pieces in.

Don't animate anything on the table but `transform` and `opacity` (the shadow on a pack past the end of its row is stepped, not animated), ease a shadow, or shake the table itself; a shake belongs to the mat, the supply and the climb's tower.
Don't put anything over the climb's picture but its bars, its subtitle, its title card and Skip, or give two cats the same pitch.

Don't magnify the match or the climb with the fit, add a quarter step to the fit, or use `xl:` and wider breakpoints on a column screen: a fitted screen is 1120px wide to itself whatever the window says. The match fits its window by layout, never by `zoom`.

Don't play a tune on the landing page, login or signup, mount the sound rig or the menu tune a second time, play an effect that the player's own action, a turn's playback, a beat of the climb or a page landing did not cause, write a note of music louder than 0.14, or ship an audio file.

Don't use gradients or emoji anywhere. Three of the four lights named under Motion are the only gradients (score heat, the legendary's shimmer, the cloth light), and each is a light, never a fill; the band that crosses a pack is flat. The sky behind the tower is a dither, not a gradient.
Don't use raster or smoothed creature art; a cat is its 16x16 sprite.

Don't use the stone greys for anything but the tower, the wall inside it, the scene it stands in and the wrapper of the Table and Tower pack, write a stone's hex where a `--color-stone*` token will do (a tower look repaints them), or draw a rival in any colour but coral. The clouds and the rock's top in the tower's scene are stone too. Don't zoom the tower by anything but a whole number (1, 2 and 32 are the ones in use), frame its stage, or fill it with anything but its scene.
Don't put anything on the tower's side of a page that is outside, let the backdrop take a click, or show a page before the camera has stopped.

Don't use an element hue for a board, a button, or a heading. The sky behind the tower is the one ground they colour and a cat pack's wrapper the one face; on a cat piece the hue is a 4px edge and never the face.
Don't set text straight on the tower's scene, smooth or blur the scene, or move any part of it in anything but whole tower pixels.
Don't use lime for anything the rival owns, or coral for a reward. The title ribbon, on the landing page and on home, is the only lime that is not the player's.

Don't show a price in money, a payment control, a paid tier or premium styling (a gold finish, a sparkle, a "best value" badge, a countdown): coins are earned by playing, packs cost coins, and nothing is sold for money. Don't show coins or a pack without the sentence that says so, and don't show how a match's coins were worked out: only what it paid and its floor's factor.
Don't let a look change how anything is built, darken a board or a cloth past what ink can be read on (7:1), light the inside of a tower, or give two packs the same print.
Don't add a save step to the wardrobe, or let a deck's change through without one.
Don't print a cost in a lane's space, write on scenery, stretch a habitat or draw it at a fraction of a pixel, or put a transform, filter, contain or container-type on `[data-match]` or above it.
